title: Bitbudget sensitivity notes: quantization tradeoff explorer
content:
Purpose
This sheet is a working calculator and playbook for exploring bitbudget tradeoffs (INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit) across three axes: cost ($/1M tokens), end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), and quality delta relative to a baseline FP16/FP32 serving profile. The goal is to provide a quick, pragmatic decision surface for engineers and product managers evaluating quantization options for different workloads.

Audience
- ML engineers who run inference and need to pick a quant profile for production
- SRE/infra who want to understand latency SLO impact
- Product/CS for cost/quality conversations with customers

High-level approach
1) Capture workload inputs: model family, parameter count, average sequence length, generation vs classification vs embedding, batch size distribution, cache hit rate (prefix reuse).
2) Use measured per-bitwidth performance coefficients (throughput multiplier, memory reduction, KV-cache growth) from microbench runs.
3) Apply task-specific quality penalty heuristics (estimated % drop in task metric e.g., logprobs/accuracy/embedding-similarity).
4) Produce combined outputs: tokens/sec, p99 latency estimate, $/1M tokens, recommended fallback strategy.

Suggested spreadsheet tabs (structure)
- Inputs: user sliders and selectors (model, seq dist, batch dist, qtypes to compare)
- Perf Profiles: measured throughput and latency multipliers per model & qtype (collected from perf lab)
- Cost Model: cloud instance / GPU hourly rate, effective utilization, concurrency penalties, amortized infra costs
- Quality Estimates: heuristics by task+bitwidth with editable cells and provenance notes
- Scenario Explorer: calculated rows for each scenario (baseline + quant variants) with deltas and color-coded flags
- Sensitivity Heatmap: delta-to-cost ratio sweep (bitwidth vs sequence length vs batch size)
- Notes & Decision Rules: human-readable heuristics for rollouts and fallbacks

Key input fields (Inputs tab)
- model_name (select): e.g., Llama-7B, Llama-13B, Mistral-7B, Redwood-20B (string)
- params_m (number): model parameter count in millions (e.g., 13000 for 13B)
- avg_seq (number): average tokens per request (e.g., 64)
- seq_95 (number): 95th percentile sequence length (optional)
- task_type (select): generation | chat | embedding | classification
- batch_mean (number): average batch size (requests aggregated)
- prefix_reuse (percentage): KV cache hit rate
- target_p99_ms (number): latency SLO to evaluate against
- cloud_gpu (select/string): instance type & cost per hour

Perf Profiles (example heuristic coefficients)
- baseline fp16 throughput = measured tokens/sec baseline (from perf lab)
- int8 throughput multiplier = baseline * 1.20–1.55 (set per model empirically)
- fp8 throughput multiplier = baseline * 1.10–1.35
- 4bit throughput multiplier = baseline * 1.3–1.9 (if kernel exists)
- memory reduction (model state) vs FP16: int8 ~ 2x, fp8 ~1.6–1.9x, 4bit ~3–4x

Quality penalty heuristics (editable)
- generation (open-ended): int8: -0.5% to -2% fluency/ROUGE/LM loss; fp8: -0.2% to -1%; 4-bit: -1.5% to -6% (depends heavily on quant scheme + calibration)
- classification/NER: int8: -0.2% to -1%; fp8: negligible to -0.5%; 4-bit: -0.5% to -3%
- embeddings: int8: ~0% to -0.3% cosine drop; fp8: ~0%; 4-bit: -0.2% to -1% (often acceptable for clustering)
Note: these are priors. Each model+task needs measurement. The sheet includes columns to attach experiment ids where these priors came from.

Derived calculations (Scenario Explorer)
- effective_tokens_per_sec = baseline_tokens_sec * throughput_multiplier * (1 + batching_effect) * cache_factor
- estimated_p99_ms = (avg_seq / effective_tokens_per_sec) * 1000 + infra_overhead_ms
- tokens_per_hour = effective_tokens_per_sec * 3600 * concurrent_slots
- cost_per_hour = instance_hourly_rate * instance_count (compute from capacity target)
- $/1M_tokens = cost_per_hour / (tokens_per_hour / 1_000_000)

Example worked scenario (illustrative numbers)
Inputs: Llama-13B, avg_seq=64, baseline_fp16_tps=1100 tokens/sec, batch_mean=1.4, prefix_reuse=30%
Perf multipliers: int8=+35% throughput, fp8=+20%, 4bit=+70% (optimistic kernel)
Outputs:
- FP16 baseline: 1100 tps, estimated p99=58ms, $/1M tokens = $6.2
- INT8: 1485 tps, estimated p99=43ms, $/1M tokens = $4.6, quality_delta = -0.9% generation
- FP8: 1320 tps, estimated p99=48ms, $/1M tokens = $5.2, quality_delta = -0.4%
- 4-bit: 1870 tps, estimated p99=36ms, $/1M tokens = $3.7, quality_delta = -2.3%
Decision notes: INT8 looks like the middle-ground for this workload: meaningful cost savings without large quality hit. 4-bit gives best cost but riskier quality — consider canary + automated evals.

Decision heuristics (starter rules)
- If expected quality delta <= 1% and p99 improves or stays within SLO => prefer INT8 as default for generation workloads.
- If embedding task and cosine drop <0.5% => prefer INT8 or FP8; prioritize FP8 if long-context and kv-cache memory matters.
- If target_p99_ms is very tight (<30ms) and model kernel supports 4-bit low-latency ops => test 4-bit but gate with regression-suite on prompt set.
- Always deploy quantized variant behind automatic fallback: if quality regression > threshold or latency spike detected, route to baseline model.

Canary and rollout checklist
- Pre-canary: run batch of 10k exemplar prompts across prompt families + compute metrics (perplexity, task acc, embedding cosine)
- Canary: run 1% production traffic for 24–72 hours with shadow logging of baseline outputs for drift detection
- Monitor: quality metric deltas, p99 latency, token-level errors, error-rates, infra GPU memory pressure
- Rollback triggers: >1.5% task-metric drop OR p99 degradation beyond SLO OR error-rate spike > x2

Open questions & next steps
- Collect standardized perf artifacts for all supported models across bitwidths (benchmark harness ticket: JIRA:INF-4123).
- Add automated cell linking to perf lab to reduce manual coefficient drift.
- Integrate this sheet with Redwood Optimize recommender pipeline (API + export format).
- Add per-customer weighting (some customers tolerate more quality drop for cost).

Notes on provenance and conservative defaults
- This sheet intentionally separates measured perf coefficients (tab controlled by infra/bench team) from quality priors (owned by applied-ml). Keep both editable but annotate origin.
- Conservative defaults in the sheet favor smaller quality deltas and lower throughput multipliers until validated.

Appendix: quick calibration steps (how to get the numbers into the sheet)
1) Run microbench on representative instance with the model and quant binaries. Report tokens/sec at target seq lengths and batch sizes.
2) Run unit quality suite: 2–5k prompts per prompt family; collect task metrics. Compute relative deltas vs FP16.
3) Measure memory footprint and KV cache growth for long-context tasks.
4) Populate Perf Profiles and Quality Estimates tabs with measured values and link the experiment ids.

If you use this sheet: please add a short note in the Notes tab with the experiment id that justified any non-default coefficients so future reviewers can trace decisions.

Maya Chen — product-optimize (draft)
